answer: A lagoon stays clear only when its water moves slowly through one channel, and an agent economy can resist fake identities the same way: each new identity must complete a sequential verifiable-delay computation that cannot be sped up by adding machines, like tracing one copper thread through an atlas of tangled routes. Every extra fake identity costs another full stretch of unskippable wall-clock time, so a thousand clones means a thousand sequential waits, while one honest agent waits once and keeps working.
